card.name: Linking words before diet or lab terms
card.fires_on: Small linking words such as 'anti' (in HBsAg and anti-HBc), 'contains' or 'containing', 'a', and 'in', placed just before a content term. The content terms are diet, food, or lab-test terms such as soybean oil, lactose, Phe-restricted diet and HBc.

modes.label: anti before -HBc
modes.description: The start of 'anti-HBc' after 'HBsAg and' in hepatitis B testing text.
modes.example: Test all patients for evidence of current or prior HBV infection by measuring HBsAg and<< anti>>-HBc before initiating HCV treatment

modes.label: Contains or containing an ingredient
modes.description: The verb 'contains' or 'containing' right before an ingredient such as soybean oil or lactose.
modes.example: KABIVEN<< contains>> soybean oil, which may cause hypers

modes.label: Other linking words before diet terms
modes.description: Short words such as 'a', 'in', or a blank space before diet, calorie or comparison wording.
modes.example: should also be treated with<< a>> Phe-restricted diet, including dietary

card.writes: Weakly favors odd fragments such as 'bar', 'pin' and 'saturated'; there is no clear link to the text.
card.plain: It fires on small linking words just before an ingredient, diet or hepatitis antibody term.
